question: If $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is defined by $f(x) = x^2+3$, which of the following is true?
explanation:
For $f(x)=x^2+3$, if $f(x_1)=f(x_2)$ then $x_1^2=x_2^2$.

This implies $x_1=\pm x_2$, so different inputs can give the same output. Hence the function is not one-one.

Also $f(x) \ge 3$ for all $x$, so negative numbers cannot be obtained as outputs. Thus the function is not onto.

Therefore the function is neither one-one nor onto.
